svg.text: SUBSURFACE GEOLOGICAL TRAPPING CHRONOLOGY & BASALTIC MINERAL CARBONATION
Multi-Century Trapping Security Evolution & In-Situ Calcite/Siderite Mineralization Kinetics (Matter et al. 2016 Science / IPCC SRCCS)
BASIS: 10,000-YEAR RESERVOIR RETENTION & RAPID BASALTIC IN-SITU SOLIDIFICATION
CAD SECTION VIEW A-A | P&ID INSTRUMENTED

g.text: CHRONOLOGICAL EVOLUTION OF GEOLOGICAL TRAPPING MECHANISMS
• Structural Trapping: Supercritical CO2 buoyancy arrested by regional caprock
• Residual Trapping: Capillary meniscus snap-off immobilizes droplets in pore network
• Solubility Trapping: Dissolution into formation water increases brine density (+1.0%),
triggering gravitational downwelling and eliminating upward pressure head
• Mineral Trapping: Geochemical reaction precipitates solid carbonate minerals;
permanent geological containment exceeding 10,000 years (> 99% retention probability)
RAPID BASALTIC MINERAL CARBONATION (CARBFIX / MATTER ET AL. 2016)
Step 1: Dissolved CO2 in Water produces Carbonic Acid
Step 2: Acid Dissolution of Basalt Silicates (Olivine, Pyroxene)
Fe2+ + CO32- => FeCO3(s) [Siderite] | Mg2+ + CO32- => MgCO3(s) [Magnesite]
AUDIT METRICS: Carbfix Conversion: >95% in <2 yrs | Water: 25 t/t | Permanent Retention
PRIMARY PROVENANCE: Matter et al. (2016) Science; IPCC SRCCS
